vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: last30days-aisa-zh
Version: 1.0.2

The last30days-zh skill is a comprehensive research tool designed to aggregate and synthesize data from various social platforms and web sources. It demonstrates high security awareness by implementing defenses against prompt injection from untrusted web content, specifically using `<untrusted_content>` tags and explicit safety warnings in `scripts/lib/rerank.py` and `scripts/lib/render.py`. While the bundle includes powerful administrative scripts like `scripts/sync.sh` (which manages file deployments across multiple agent directories) and `scripts/compare.sh` (which uses risky execution flags), these are clearly aligned with the developer's stated purpose for testing and deployment. The skill handles sensitive credentials (AISA_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN) and supports webhook notifications in `scripts/watchlist.py`, but all behaviors appear legitimate and well-documented.

llm.summary: The skill's requested binaries and single primary credential (AISA_API_KEY) match its stated aggregator/analysis purpose; it persists research data to user home paths and contains convenience scripts that may copy files to local plugin caches, which are expected for this type of tool but worth noting before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description: last30days aggregates recent social, community, market, GitHub and grounded web results. Declared runtime needs (python3, bash, AISA_API_KEY) line up with included code that calls AISA for planning/search and runs Python scripts for retrieval, ranking, and storage. Optional GitHub tokens are referenced in SKILL.md and code (GitHub access is optional and not declared as required), which is coherent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and included scripts instruct the agent to run Python/bash scripts that perform web calls (AISA and provider-specific APIs), persist full result dumps and transcripts to ~/.local/share/last30days and optionally other user directories, and offer utilities (sync.sh, compare.sh) that copy files into $HOME plugin caches. Reading and writing files and performing web requests is within the tool's purpose (collecting and storing research), but users should be aware these files (including full transcripts) are written to disk and some helper scripts may touch plugin caches if run.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction+code with no external install spec. All code is bundled in the package; there are no remote downloads or extract-from-URL steps. That lowers install-time risk compared to network-based installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only AISA_API_KEY is required as the primary credential (used for planning, search, and judge calls). GitHub tokens (GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN) are optional and only used when the user requests GitHub API functionality. The set of env vars requested is proportional to the aggregated-research purpose; no unrelated credentials are demanded.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a SQLite DB and saved output files under the user's home (~/.local/share/last30days and saved output dirs). That persistent storage is expected for a watchlist/briefing tool, but it means research results and transcripts will remain on disk. Helper scripts (sync.sh, compare.sh) can copy files into $HOME/.claude/plugins, $HOME/.agents/skills, etc., if explicitly run — users should avoid running these sync utilities unless they understand the target locations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent for its stated purpose, but review these before installing or running: 1) It requires an AISA_API_KEY which the code uses for planning/search/judge requests — provide a dedicated key you can revoke if needed. 2) It persists complete research dumps and transcripts to ~/.local/share/last30days and may write saved output to Documents or other user dirs — expect persistent local storage of collected content. 3) Optional GitHub tokens are used only for GitHub API access; you don't need to set them unless you use that feature. 4) The repo includes helper scripts (sync.sh, compare.sh) that, if run, copy files into local plugin caches ($HOME/.claude/plugins, $HOME/.agents/skills, etc.) and invoke local CLIs; do not run those unless you intend to modify those locations. 5) If you are concerned about data exfiltration or mixing data, run the skill in an isolated account/container or use a scoped/dedicated AISA key and avoid running sync utilities. Finally, if you want additional assurance, inspect env/config handling (scripts/lib/env.py and setup_wizard) to confirm where credentials and config are written and consider rotating the AISA key after testing.
